operation_tail.detail: Current coverage, checker limits, planned deployments, infrastructure index, ONSPD semantics and the official fixed broadband ZIP asset route were rechecked.
Official 32.2 MB asset route resolved, but this environment could not resolve or transfer the binary.
Panel resolves all 23 SHA-pinned chunks without copying source payloads.
No live owner, active PENDING, duplicate task or second runner.
New downloader safely fetches the official archive on the canonical Windows host.
Download failure is captured by the combined orchestrator without terminating the parent PowerShell session.
017 now attempts the official download automatically when the cache is absent.
Successful envelope download is handed to the existing inner-r2 CRC/schema/row validator.
Both automation scripts were read back from the canonical branch.
DNS and binary-transfer failures were recorded without promoting any candidate.
Runtime, manual-action and web-visible operation state were synchronized.
The official Connected Nations Spring 2026 publication page was reachable and parsed on 2026-07-25.
The official page identifies 13 May 2026 as the publication date.
The publication describes coverage and availability as of January 2026.
The official page exposes the fixed broadband coverage and full-fibre take-up ZIP as a 32.2 MB download.
The source covers fixed-line and fixed-wireless availability; this remains an area-level postcode proxy, not a parcel measurement.
The 82% full-fibre figure is a UK residential-premises aggregate and is not promoted to any parcel row.
The 89% gigabit-capable figure is a UK aggregate and is not promoted to any parcel row.
The official download section links to Ofcom terms of use; archive attribution and licence evidence remain required at binary readback.
Ofcom states the collected data updates its coverage checkers, but checker output is not substituted for corrected r2 archive rows.
The planned-deployment report concerns expected coverage to the end of 2028 and is excluded from current January 2026 parcel coverage claims.
The official ZIP route was resolved again, but this environment still could not transfer binary bytes; no repeated task or runner was started.
Official coverage candidates, measured parcel speeds and 3/4 accuracy remain zero until exact corrected inner-r2 CRC/schema/row validation passes on the canonical host.
Spring 2026 fixed broadband reporting covers availability from fixed-line and fixed-wireless networks; it is not evidence of an active connection or measured parcel throughput.
Gigabit and full-fibre coverage headline figures focus on residential properties, while take-up and some decent-broadband statistics include all premises; denominators are not mixed into parcel rows.
The 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload decent-broadband threshold is regulatory context and is not written as a measured candidate speed.
The broadband checker describes speeds as the fastest estimated speeds predicted by network operators and warns that actual property availability or speeds may differ.
Checker green, amber and red availability states describe general or partial area availability and are not substituted for corrected postcode archive records.
Checker updates do not supply the versioned corrected inner-r2 files, CRCs and schema evidence required by the strict archive join.
Ofcom FAQs state that the fixed performance postcode file is no longer published and that current performance analysis is sufficiently robust down to local-authority level, not postcode level.
ONSPD includes both current and terminated postcodes; terminated records remain review-only rather than being promoted as live coverage candidates.
ONSPD assigns a postcode to an area using a point-in-polygon result based on the mean grid reference of addresses, so it is not exact property geometry.
ONS confirms that postcode products are released quarterly in February, May, August and November.
The one-metre grid-reference product resolution does not turn a postcode centroid into a measured premise or parcel location.
The public Connected Nations catalogue was rechecked with an 8 July 2026 update date; it remains catalogue evidence rather than the corrected Spring 2026 binary payload.
The catalogue lists no specific licence, so archive use must continue to rely on Ofcom's own terms and attribution evidence.
The planned deployment report is based on operators' stated plans as of January 2026 and is excluded from current-coverage candidates.
The expired ownership lease and terminal PUBLISHED heartbeat were rechecked; no duplicate task, second runner or stuck active PENDING was created.
Sixteen additional official methodology and scope checks were published to the line-by-line panel while official 3/4 candidates and parcel speed measurements remained zero.
